bindings.label: Patient experienced post-procedural abdominal pain, nausea, and elevated body temperature (maximum 37.8°C)

66-year-old female with history of Hashimoto's thyroiditis and thrombocytopenia; routine blood tests over years showed leukocytopenia and thrombocytopenia; initial blood test showed leukocyte count 3.16×10^9/L and platelet count 109.00×10^9/L; no other symptoms and no significant abnormalities in cardiac enzymes or blood coagulation

Four hours post-procedure, patient developed intermittent abdominal pain and occasional nausea; nine hours post-operation, right abdomen pain recurred and progressed to involve the entire abdomen, with persistent nausea and perceived increase in body temperature
Initial physical examination showed tenderness in right abdomen without rebound tenderness or muscular tension and with normal bowel sounds

Later physical examination showed diffuse tenderness with rebound tenderness mainly in right abdomen, dullness to percussion, no liver percussion pain, negative shifting dullness, and normal bowel sounds; maximum body temperature was 37.8°C
CT shows edematous thickening of ascending colon with exudative changes and small ascites, without perforation signs or free air
CRP is 2.45 mg/L and PCT is 0.58 ng/ml, showing mild inflammatory elevation
CT shows no significant intra-abdominal fluid or blood accumulation suggestive of hemorrhage
Laboratory results show neutrophilia in the setting of baseline leukocytopenia
